requirements.title: SPACING result follows the real model with zero and IEEE special cases
requirements.definition: For finite nonzero X, SPACING returns the 16.4 model spacing near X subject to representability and tie rules; zero returns TINY(X), IEEE infinity returns an IEEE NaN, and IEEE NaN returns that NaN.

pending.SPACING-finite-nonzero-model-value: Initialize default-real and double-precision result sentinels to -1.0, then assert SPACING(1.0)==EPSILON(1.0). For concrete normal model inputs 3.0, -0.75, and 1024.0 in each kind, assert SPACING(x)==SCALE(1.0_same_kind, EXPONENT(x)-DIGITS(x)) and SPACING(-x)==SPACING(x); mutate the SCALE exponent or sign-pair operand so the relation checks fail. Do not assert hard-coded processor model constants such as a decimal or binary spacing value.
pending.SPACING-finite-nonzero-positive: Initialize a real result to -1.0, assign SPACING(1.0) and SPACING(3.0), assert each result is positive and at least TINY of the same kind, and mutate the intrinsic to return the sentinel so the bounded check fails.
pending.SPACING-zero-same-as-TINY: Initialize a real result to HUGE(0.0), assign SPACING(0.0), assert it equals TINY(0.0) exactly, and use SPACING(1.0) as a nonzero companion.
pending.SPACING-ieee-infinity-returns-NaN: Use IEEE_ARITHMETIC support probes as admission guards, create positive infinity with IEEE_VALUE, initialize a logical sentinel to .false., and assert IEEE_IS_NAN(SPACING(infinity)); no claim is made on processors lacking IEEE support.
pending.SPACING-ieee-NaN-returns-NaN: Use IEEE_ARITHMETIC support probes as admission guards, create a quiet NaN with IEEE_VALUE, initialize a logical sentinel to .false., and assert IEEE_IS_NAN(SPACING(qnan)); NaN payload identity is not used as an oracle.
pending.SPACING-ieee-NaN-identity: No portable identity oracle exists for the words that NaN: IEEE NaN payload and sign preservation are not exposed portably across processors, so future fixtures may observe only the NaN class.
